> 三世诸佛，依般若波罗蜜多故，得阿耨多罗三藐三菩提。

Two lines earlier the sutra said 无智亦无得 — no wisdom, no attainment. Now it says the buddhas of past, present and future, relying on prajna, attain supreme awakening.

If you read that as a contradiction, you are reading it correctly. It is a contradiction on purpose, and it is the sutra's most compressed lesson in how the vocabulary of attainment works.

## Two kinds of 得

The book separates them, and the separation is the whole content of the line.

First: acquisition. There is a gap in me — I am not yet awakened — and practice is the payment, and awakening is the goods. This is 有取之得, attainment by taking. It is exactly what 无智亦无得 removed, because it depends on a deficient self being supplied from outside.

Second: 消障而显之得. Not acquiring something new — removing what covered it over. The buddhas did not gain awakening; the coverings came off.

The book's image: cloud cover and open sky. When the clouds disperse, the sky appears. Nobody would say the sky was produced by the dispersal. 云散之后虚空现前 — and the sky was never absent, only obscured.

Which is why the two statements do not fight. The first denies acquisition. The second uses the same verb for a different operation, and the sutra does not stop to explain, because the explanation would take a page and the reader who has followed the previous lines already has it.

## 三世 is not a timeline

Three times: past, present, future. Read literally it puts the buddhas inside history, which makes awakening a dated event and puts you outside it.

The book's gloss moves it: 三世 is the framework of sequence itself — the way attention is built to arrange experience as before, now, after. Being locked in that framework is the ordinary condition. Naming all three times together is a way of saying this law is not tied to an era, a culture, or a capacity.

So the sentence covers everything by covering the frame everything appears in.

## 阿耨多罗三藐三菩提, unpacked

Four parts, and each one removes a comparison.

阿耨多罗 — unsurpassed. There is no higher level, because the scale that would rank levels has been dissolved.
三藐 — perfectly equal. No seam between self and other, between awakened and deluded. Not equality as a value; equality as the absence of a boundary that would permit ranking.
三菩提 — right awakening. Seeing as it is, without addition, distortion, or the manufacture of an extra preference.

Read the three together and the term stops being a title and becomes a description of a mind with no edges left to compare across.

## What the line does not promise

It does not promise that you will get there. It says: this is what the word has always meant, and the meaning is not an event.

The book is blunt about the consequence: after the fact, there is no one who relied, no dharma relied upon, and no awakening obtained. All three are provisional names. What continues is the functioning — 随缘应化的作用不坏 — which is why the sutra can empty out every term and still be a sutra.

## The test

Take a competence you are proud of and describe how you got it. Then notice how much of the story is acquisition — effort, practice, accumulation — and how much is removal: a misunderstanding that stopped, a fear that stopped steering, a habit that stopped firing.

Most skilled people can report the first half in detail and have never once counted the second.
